{"consolidated_memory":"RECURRING SIGNATURE MISMATCH IN KEY ROTATION — crypto/keys/rotation.py

All incidents involved the same fundamental problem: signature mismatch in key rotation, triggered by rotating the signing key while requests are in flight. The signal in every case was a verification failure against the previous key. Stack: Python. Covering test: tests/crypto/test_rotation.py. All fixes deployed via PR branches named fix/signature-mismatch-N.

OCCASION 1: [2026-01-11]
Trigger condition: jobs scheduled across the midnight boundary
Root cause: missing composite index on (tenant_id, created_at)
Fix: added the composite index and backfilled in batches (PR #2790, branch fix/signature-mismatch-1)
Result: throughput rose 28 percent, to 175 requests per second

OCCASION 2: [2026-02-19]
Trigger condition: input list came in empty
Root cause: a listener registered but never removed
Fix: removed the listener on teardown and asserted it in a test (PR #3028, branch fix/signature-mismatch-2)
Result: the alert stayed quiet for 73 consecutive days

OCCASION 3: [2026-03-15]
Trigger condition: accounts in the five percent rollout bucket
Root cause: a mutable default argument shared across calls
Fix: made the default empty and built the value per call (PR #4011, branch fix/signature-mismatch-3)
Result: the job finished in 85 minutes instead of 3 hours

OCCASION 4: [2026-04-21]
Trigger condition: two requests raced on the same key
Root cause: an N+1 query hidden behind a lazy relation
Fix: prefetched the relation in a single query (PR #4575, branch fix/signature-mismatch-4)
Result: the flaky test went from 60 failures per hundred runs to zero

OCCASION 5: [2026-04-27]
Trigger condition: sessions that arrived through the OAuth provider
Root cause: missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
Fix: normalised to NFC ahead of the digest (PR #5430, branch fix/signature-mismatch-5)
Result: memory settled at 818 MB instead of climbing past 9 GB

OCCASION 6: [2026-04-29]
Trigger condition: payloads above roughly two megabytes
Root cause: a cache entry that was never invalidated on write
Fix: invalidated the entry inside the write transaction (PR #7626, branch fix/signature-mismatch-6)
Result: the backlog cleared 65 minutes after the deploy

OCCASION 7: [2026-05-29]
Trigger condition: users sitting in a negative UTC offset
Root cause: clock skew between the two hosts
Fix: switched the deadline to a monotonic clock (PR #9555, branch fix/signature-mismatch-7)
Result: we reclaimed 44 GB of blob storage

OCCASION 8: [2026-07-13]
Trigger condition: client had already retried once
Root cause: a naive datetime compared against an aware one
Fix: made every boundary timezone aware at the edge (PR #9732, branch fix/signature-mismatch-8)
Result: p99 latency fell from 3.5 s to 228 ms"}
